name: Shepherd's purse
habitat: Disturbed ground everywhere — gardens, waste ground, cracks in pavement, field margins. One of the most common weeds on Earth.
identify: THE MARK: flat, heart-shaped or triangular seed pods held out from the stem on little stalks, like tiny purses. Unmistakable once seen.
Basal rosette of deeply lobed dandelion-ish leaves; stem leaves clasp the stem and are much smaller.
Tiny white four-petalled flowers at the top of the stem while pods ripen below — flowers and pods are on the plant at the same time.

lookalikes.name: Field pennycress
lookalikes.danger: Low — also a mustard, not toxic in passing contact, but a different plant with different action.
lookalikes.tell: Pennycress pods are ROUND and flat like coins, notched at the top; shepherd's purse pods are triangular hearts.

lookalikes.name: Other white-flowered mustards
lookalikes.danger: Low; the mustard family holds no deadly members in temperate regions, which makes this an unusually forgiving plant to learn.
lookalikes.tell: The purse-shaped pod is diagnostic. Without pods, wait until it fruits.

preparations.method: Crush the fresh whole plant and press onto the bleeding area.
preparations.for_use: Slowing bleeding from a shallow wound or a nosebleed.

preparations.method: Steep the fresh or recently dried plant in hot water 10 minutes.
preparations.for_use: The traditional internal styptic — used in European and Chinese medicine for heavy menstrual and postpartum bleeding.

cautions: The hemostatic activity is strongly reduced by drying and storage; old dried material is close to inert. Fresh is what the tradition uses.
Avoid in pregnancy — it is a traditional uterine stimulant.
Reported to raise blood pressure and to interact with sedatives, thyroid medication, and anticoagulants.
For a serious bleed the answer is pressure, not a plant.
evidence: Long documented use as a styptic in both European and East Asian traditions, and it remains a listed herbal medicine in several pharmacopoeias. Modern controlled evidence is limited and mixed.
